reviews.decision_reason: select_demand is described as using a score threshold while keeping explicit fallback identifiers, but the visible source selects every corpus record with demand_score >= 3, which includes all 8 supplied records. That over-selects generic or lower-priority candidates and relies on normalize to truncate later, so the boundary does not itself enforce the required deterministic demand recommendation.

normalize returns only retained_df.head(len(index_window)) with index_window = [0]. That drops seven selected demand records by position rather than by market-demand support, making downstream output depend on prior row order instead of a defensible demand filter. It also masks the over-selection from select_demand by reducing the normalized handoff to one row.

assemble_provenance performs missing-safe access and deterministic ordering over the normalized needs it receives, and its one-row evidence_sources output is consistent with the one-row normalized input. The loss of demand records is already present before this boundary.
